01 - Adea PRD: product vision, users, requirements, scope, UX, business model, and roadmap-level requirements.

02 - Control Plane PRD: open-source execution-platform vision, consumers, product promise, capabilities, optional provider-neutral context/memory integration model, standalone requirements, packaging, and roadmap-level requirements.

03 - Cortana PRD: open-source local-first knowledge and memory product vision, users, product promise, scope, UX, durable functional requirements, provider-specific ContextBundle/memory behavior, security and optional integration boundaries, and acceptance criteria.
04 - System Architecture Overview: concise end-to-end architecture, repository boundaries, composition model, trust boundaries, and component relationships for technical and non-technical readers.

Adea TDD: implementation of the desktop-first Adea application, canonical Channel/Message conversation timeline, shared Three.js spatial and Slack-style conventional clients, encrypted local ContentRef store, optional E2E ContentReplica cross-device history synchronization, Local Runtime Host, E2E web/mobile remote relay, cloud-safe workspaces/Tasks/Channels, Railway Event Gateway, billing presentation, explicit R2 Artifact promotion/scanning, and Control Plane integration.

Control Plane TDD: implementation of one portable TypeScript Control Plane core across Local, Self-hosted `simple`, Self-hosted `server`, and the managed-cloud profile (the M9 Railway/Neon/R2/Restate reference, already implemented and certified): deterministic AgentProfile/Skill and ContextProvider resolution, immutable ExecutionPlans, ProjectState/ContextPackages, Restate lifecycle, SQLite/PostgreSQL PersistenceProvider, DirectLocalRuntimeTransport and Runtime Gateway only for non-co-located runtimes, SecretsProvider/ObjectStore ports, managed Pi/ACP, tools/models/sandboxes, LangGraph orchestration, usage, and evals.

Cortana TDD: implementation of the independent local-first Cortana product: source ingestion, canonical evidence/code, single-node SQLite, embeddings, hybrid retrieval, native memory, context compilation, Desktop/MCP/HTTP/CLI, supported Local and Self-hosted/VPS profiles, standalone provider conformance, operations, and optional first-party integration.
Agent & Skill Specification: canonical schemas and rules for Agent Profiles, Skills, Capabilities, precedence, conflict resolution, and runtime translation.

Data Model & API Specification: canonical entities, identifiers, Channel/Message and ContentRef/ContentReplica contracts, ContentSyncDevice and ContentKeyEpoch/ContentKeyEnvelope synchronization contracts, RuntimeNode/RuntimeConnection and ContextProvider relationships, state machines, runtime/session/provider-reference contracts, API contracts, event schemas, and cross-service interfaces.

RuntimeNode & Desktop Protocol Specification: canonical ownership, pairing, separate Ed25519 authentication/signing and RuntimeNode X25519 E2E remote-content keys, ContentSyncDevice separation, Adea Remote Relay versus Runtime Gateway versus durable ContentReplica synchronization distinction, DirectLocalRuntimeTransport/RuntimeDriver/Tauri privileges, Self-hosted nodes, operational command defaults, HPKE transport envelope, and LocalProjectGrant contracts.

Execution Consistency & Event Delivery Specification: canonical command outbox/inbox, idempotency, reconciliation, durable Message/ContentReplica mutation semantics, transient streaming-delta separation, EventInbox, WorkspaceEvent sequencing, SSE gateway, and ProjectState concurrency contracts.

Artifact Storage Specification: canonical Artifact identity/metadata, Local/Self-hosted default byte ownership, explicit Cloudflare R2 promotion, upload/download capability TTLs and size lanes, integrity/type checks, replaceable MalwareScanner with initial ClamAV implementation, quarantine, retention, and deletion contracts.

Security & Trust Model: trust boundaries, encrypted Adea local content, E2E ContentReplica synchronization, ContentSyncDevice and ContentKeyEnvelope lifecycle, deployment-profile SecretsProvider, separate RuntimeNode signing/encryption keys, HPKE remote control, direct/local versus remote runtime/provider boundaries, Artifact malware scanning, provider scope/memory-write safety, workspace isolation, retention, and threat model.

Evaluation & Benchmarking Plan: quality, cost, latency, reliability, deployment/persistence/RuntimeTransport conformance, privacy/HPKE, Artifact scanner/promotion behavior, profile/Skill/runtime/context-provider comparisons, no-provider portability, memory-write safety, resource budgets, and rollout criteria.

Agent HQ reimagines how humans collaborate with multi-agent AI systems by turning abstract automation into a spatial, gamified management experience to combat dashboard fatigue.
Inspired by top-down co-working platforms and cozy simulation games, Agent HQ provides an intuitive interface to assign, monitor, and collaborate with specialized AI agents.
Agent HQ is designed to make powerful agent workflows accessible to both advanced and non-technical users and teams.
Agent HQ adds an opinionated Control Plane above the rapidly evolving agent ecosystem rather than building another proprietary agent harness.

Fast, Functional UX: quick point-and-click navigation, clear spatial awareness, and lightweight UI overlays.
Core workspace functions should remain reachable without unnecessary movement or scene changes.
Dual Environment Focus:
Business Workspaces: Dedicated office rooms, seating areas, interactive Kanban boards, and work desks for team and agent orchestration.
Spatial Home: Cozy apartment/home environments (study, living room, pantry) designed for daily personal automation - managing personal finances, meal planning, travel booking, and routine scheduling.

Dual Workspace & Communication Surfaces: The Three.js spatial workspace is the primary experience, while a familiar Slack-style channel/list interface is a first-class secondary workspace for information-dense collaboration.
Both surfaces operate on the same Rooms, Channels, persistent Agents, Tasks, and durable Message timeline rather than separate conversation systems.
Users can move between room/channel conversations, direct Agent conversations, threads/replies, mentions, attachments, and task references without losing context.
Voice, spatial audio, and video zones remain later enhancements.
Role & Character Assignment: Give persistent Agents distinct avatars and personas for roles such as Lead Developer, Marketing Specialist, Personal Finance Assistant, or Daily Scheduler.
Delegated Workers can appear temporarily when that visibility helps the user understand what is happening.
Space Customization: Users can arrange rooms, furniture, and tools to match their brand or personal style.
Developers Facing "Dashboard Fatigue"
Engagement Problem: Flat chat and dashboard interfaces make it difficult to see who is doing what across a growing set of agents and tasks.
Value: Spatial organization and lightweight progression make agent activity easier to follow and give users a stronger sense of momentum.
Ordinary Consumers & Personal Life Automators
Persona: Everyday non-technical consumers who want to automate daily personal chores, finances, and scheduling without writing code or navigating dry spreadsheets.
Value: A familiar home layout gives personal Agents clear roles and makes recurring life-admin tasks easier to understand and manage.
Non-Technical Entrepreneurs & Small Businesses

Persona: Non-technical founders who want to contribute to the automation of their business operations (accounting, marketing, outreach) but are intimidated by terminal commands or complex configurations.
Value: Turning abstract agent configuration into opinionated, plug-and-play roles makes complex automation faster and easier to set up.
Multi-Venture Founders & Creators

Agent HQ launches desktop-first and local-first for developers who already work with local repositories, terminals, coding harnesses, tools, and project environments.
The Tauri 2 desktop application is the full Agent HQ experience and packages/supervises the local Control Plane, Restate runtime, optional Cortana, managed Pi, and required local runtime components.
Co-located execution uses direct RuntimeAdapter/RuntimeDriver transport rather than a cloud round trip.
Agent HQ Remote Relay is used when web/mobile controls a selected Local/Self-hosted Control Plane
Runtime Gateway is reserved only for a different/non-co-located RuntimeNode.
A Self-hosted Control Plane and runtime that are co-located use the same direct-driver semantics as the desktop profile.
Local project access is limited to explicit LocalProjectGrants, and work is never silently moved to another environment when the selected execution location is unavailable.
Web and mobile clients are companion surfaces for the same synchronized workspace and canonical Agent HQ conversation timeline.

Knowledge needed by agents is fragmented across note applications, cloud documents, email, calendars, chat systems, repositories, local files, and harness-specific histories.
Users repeatedly copy context between tools, pay to re-embed unchanged content, lose provenance, and cannot reliably determine which source or memory an answer used.

Existing knowledge products primarily serve humans, while agent-memory products often preserve conclusions without owning the complete source corpus, code index, human browsing experience, local operations surface, deletion semantics, and authorization boundary.
Cortana closes that gap by owning canonical evidence, explicit native memory, and the deterministic context handoff between them.
The product must solve this without turning the user's machine into an unrestricted crawler or silently moving private data into a hosted system.

A new user should be able to install Cortana Desktop, create a workspace, approve one source, run a bounded read-only validation, confirm a small non-reconciling trial, browse the resulting canonical document, and ask one cited question without first learning connector internals, embedding infrastructure, MCP, SQLite, or service managers.
A new installation starts query-only.
Authorization, source reads, embedding work, indexing, reconciliation, recurring synchronization, shared-agent access, cloud-provider use, and native-memory writes are separate explicit decisions.
Once configured, the same private brain should serve the user's supported agents without duplicating the corpus or allowing one harness to become the source of truth for the others.
Developers and technical operators who use Pi, Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, or other supported clients and need one reusable source of code, project knowledge, and durable preferences.
Founders and multi-project operators who need clear separation among work, personal, and special contexts, including distinct source accounts, credentials, memories, and ACL scopes.
Privacy-sensitive knowledge workers who want local ownership, explicit data movement, provider choice, reliable backup and restore, and inspectable citations.
AI agents and orchestration systems that need a narrow, token-bounded, revision-aware context interface rather than unrestricted access to a user's complete corpus.
Operators responsible for source authorization, validation, service health, release integrity, recovery, and production activation.

Evidence is source-backed knowledge.

Evidence authority comes from stable source identity.
Evidence authority comes from canonical content.
Evidence authority comes from provenance.
Evidence authority comes from update time.
Evidence authority comes from workspace scope.
Evidence authority comes from ACL.
Native memory is a bounded conclusion deliberately written by a user or authorized agent.

The memory stack below describes information authority, retention, and use.
World knowledge: source-backed knowledge and code preserved as evidence and organized across workspaces and agents.
Operational memory: what an agent should remember about the user, the way work is performed, prior experiences, and active work.
Task-local scratchpad: temporary reasoning or execution state owned by the current harness or task.

Derived context: a temporary ContextBundle assembled from authorized evidence and operational memory for one objective.
Content type: semantic, episodic, procedural, and preference describe what a durable memory means.

Cortana's native memory layer remains independently useful, while engine-like behavior must be bounded, approval-aware, provenance-bearing, and evaluated before activation.
The public write command is remember.
Retain is the broader lifecycle term for committing a reviewed bounded conclusion.
Reflect means synthesized reasoning over recalled memory
Reflection is derived output and cannot mutate canonical memory without a separate approved retain/remember operation.
Local-first and approval-gated: data stays local by default, and every source, provider, schedule, remote principal, and destructive operation requires an explicit trust decision.
Evidence before synthesis: canonical source records and citations remain inspectable even when a query model is unavailable or disabled.
Memory is not ingestion: source documents and transcripts are never silently promoted into native memory.
Context is compiled, not accumulated: agents receive the smallest useful bounded bundle instead of the full corpus or parent transcript.
Safe degradation is required: embedding failure falls back to lexical retrieval; planning or synthesis failure falls back to deterministic extractive behavior; uncertain reconciliation fails closed.
One core across surfaces: Desktop, MCP, HTTP, and CLI share the same store, authorization, retrieval, memory, and operational contracts.
Derived state is reproducible: corpus revision, memory revision, embedding generation, source configuration, and policy changes invalidate caches and stale results.
Independent deployment: Agent HQ and the Control Plane integrate through versioned interfaces and never read Cortana's database or inherit its credentials.
Users configure named sources inside a workspace, authorize the minimum required account or host permission, validate a bounded read-only snapshot, and then explicitly approve ingestion.
Stable source and source_id values preserve identity across runs.
Complete snapshots may reconcile deletions only after current full-budget validation

First launch: install the supported Desktop package, approve only required optional tooling, create a workspace, configure an embedding provider, and reach a healthy query-only state.

Source rollout: add a source, authorize it, validate it read-only, inspect scope and budgets, run a small no-reconcile trial, review citations and operational behavior, then separately approve any larger or recurring policy.
Knowledge use: browse canonical documents, search within a workspace or source, inspect backlinks or nearby records, and request cited context or an extractive answer.
Memory use: retain one bounded conclusion through the remember operation, recall it when relevant, use expiry for working state, supersede changed conclusions, and redact when withdrawn.
Reflection may synthesize from recalled memory but remains derived output unless separately retained.

Agent use: connect through MCP or scoped HTTP, request the narrowest ContextBundle that can satisfy the task, preserve evidence citations, and avoid broad source reads unless exact source access is required.
Recovery: inspect readiness and source status, verify a backup, restore only after explicit confirmation, preserve a recovery copy, and revalidate before resuming ingestion.

MVP node types are local_device and remote_host.
agent_hq_cloud is added with later managed consumer offering.
RuntimeConnection identifies a concrete harness/runtime on a RuntimeNode.
Switching execution location preserves core Control Plane functionality and semantics.
Unavailable Local/Self-hosted work is never silently moved to Agent HQ Cloud.
Agent HQ keeps a stable product-owned user_id independent from authentication-provider subjects.
Neon Auth remains behind @agent-hq/auth
workspace authorization resolves the Agent HQ User and explicit permissions server-side.
Remote-origin state-changing execution crosses Agent HQ and Control Plane through the durable Agent HQ relay/CommandOutbox.
The Control Plane CommandInbox receives remote-origin state-changing execution.
Co-located desktop submission may enter CommandInbox directly.
Co-located desktop submission does not require a cloud outbox hop.
Content-bearing remote requests use the HPKE envelope.
Content-bearing remote results use the HPKE envelope.
Control Plane cloud-safe events enter Agent HQ through a deduplicating EventInbox.
Agent HQ commits product metadata and WorkspaceEvents transactionally after EventInbox deduplication.
Platform records are idempotent under stable keys.
RuntimeDrivers propagate idempotency where supported.
RuntimeDrivers reconcile authoritative downstream status where supported.
Ambiguous non-idempotent external effects stop automatic retry.
Ambiguous non-idempotent external effects enter reconciliation_required.
WorkspaceEvents are ordered by workspace_sequence in Agent HQ Neon and delivered through Railway Event Gateway over SSE.
Cursor v1 is an HMAC-authenticated opaque cursor.
Online replay window is at least 30 days.
Heartbeat is 15 seconds.
Replay pages are bounded at 500 events.
PostgreSQL LISTEN/NOTIFY carries event identity/sequence only with 2-second polling fallback.
Reconnect and scale-out correctness always come from Neon replay.
Local project access uses LocalProjectGrant metadata plus node-local encrypted path mapping.
Agent HQ Desktop private Task/Message/execution bodies use separate AES-256-GCM local SQLite content store.
Local content root key remains in OS-secure storage.
Cloud product records use opaque ContentRefs.
ContentRef may remain local-only.
With explicit policy, E2E agent_hq_e2ee_sync ContentReplica ciphertext may be stored in Agent HQ Cloud.
ContentKeyEpoch is wrapped only to authorized ContentSyncDevices through ContentKeyEnvelopes.
Execution commands reference grants/ContentRefs rather than arbitrary absolute paths.

Repositories, ContextPackages, ProjectState, Cortana memory, credentials, artifacts, local-only bodies, synchronized plaintext, and unwrapped keys are not copied to Agent HQ Cloud merely for remote control/history sync.
Durable files/outputs use stable workspace-scoped Artifact records and provider-neutral storage boundaries.
Local/Self-hosted uses local filesystem/object storage by default.
Cloudflare R2 is private S3-compatible cloud-byte provider for explicitly promoted Artifacts.
Application integrity/version/quarantine/retention controls remain authoritative.
Adapter does not assume AWS KMS, Object Lock, or full S3 semantics.
Promotion fails closed until integrity passes.
Detected media type/file-class policy must pass.
Required replaceable MalwareScanner checks must pass before availability.
ClamAV is the initial isolated first-party scanner.
Ordinary promotion limit is 100 MiB.
Explicit multipart lane limit is 1 GiB.
Upload capabilities expire after 15 minutes.
Download capabilities expire after 5 minutes.
Local/external Artifacts may remain references and are never copied automatically.
The RuntimeNode & Desktop Protocol Specification, Execution Consistency & Event Delivery Specification, and Artifact Storage Specification define the exact contracts.

A Capability is a normalized requirement independent from a particular implementation.

Runtime Adapters determine whether and how a concrete managed or external runtime can satisfy each requirement.
Current intended precedence, highest to lowest:
Resolution precedence 1 is platform security/global invariants.
Resolution precedence 2 is workspace policy and permission constraints.
Resolution precedence 3 is approved AgentProfile hard constraints/invariants.
Resolution precedence 4 is explicit task instructions and user-selected runtime constraints.
Resolution precedence 5 is AgentProfile defaults plus workspace-specific Agent overrides.
Resolution precedence 6 is task-time skill/capability augmentation.
Resolution precedence 7 is harness-native/project configuration where applicable.
Resolution is deterministic and provenance-bearing.

Lower-priority layers cannot broaden higher-priority security, tool, model, context, runtime-location, permission, budget, or hard-instruction authority.
Hard constraints are non-overridable below platform/workspace policy.
Permitted defaults may be replaced only by explicit higher-precedence task/user inputs.
Resolver provenance includes every input layer, merge decision, selected Skill version, conflict/supersedes decision, and resulting digest.
The Control Plane resolves the smallest explicit Skill set required by the execution.
MVP selection is deterministic and does not use semantic/LLM auto-discovery.
The resolved set contains the pinned AgentProfile baseline, explicit authorized task-time Skill requests, and transitive declared dependencies.
resolve each dependency by skill_id plus SemVer range and select the highest published, approved/trusted, non-prerelease compatible version satisfying every accumulated range
resolve dependencies as a DAG;
cycles and unsatisfied ranges fail before execution
treat an explicit conflicts relationship as invalid when both Skills are selected unless an explicit supersedes relationship resolves the pair
use deterministic topological ordering with stable skill_id then SemVer tie-breakers where dependency order does not decide ordering
pin exact skill_version_id and content_digest values plus resolution provenance in the ExecutionPlan
accept system-curated, workspace-authorized, and private/user-authorized Skills under recorded provenance/trust metadata;
public community marketplace ingestion is not an MVP input
Existing external harnesses may already contain native skills, project instructions, plugins, MCP servers, tools, and permissions.
Enabling ACP (Agent Client Protocol) must not automatically rewrite these environments.
The Control Plane may pass temporary task/context instructions only through Runtime Adapter capabilities the harness actually supports.
Persistent installation or mutation requires explicit user action.
Resolved Agent configuration stays runtime-independent and deployment-location-independent.
A Control Plane-owned Runtime Adapter translates the supported subset into the target harness, reports negotiated/known capabilities, and normalizes runtime-specific errors and results.
ACP is one interoperability protocol used by external-harness adapters;
Restate workflows/operations, LangGraph graph nodes, and Agent HQ consume normalized Control Plane/runtime/tool contracts rather than speaking ACP or provider APIs directly.
Unsupported fields/capabilities must be surfaced explicitly and make a runtime ineligible when they are required.
Every execution records the exact AgentProfile and Skill versions used.
Published AgentProfile executable versions are immutable monotonically increasing positive integer versions with independent schema version and content digest.
Skills use SemVer plus immutable skill_version_id, revision, and content digest;
SemVer build metadata does not alter precedence and prerelease versions are never selected automatically for approved/default execution.
The immutable ExecutionPlan pins the resolved profile version, ordered Skill manifest, capability/tool policy, ContextPackage version, and relevant runtime/model constraints.
Changes create new versions.
Deprecation, revocation, or supersession never rewrites historical execution records.
Profile and Skill promotion should be backed by task suites measuring quality, cost, latency, tool success, failure recovery, and context overhead.
Runtime-specific translation should have compatibility tests.

Skill dependency resolution produces a deterministic ordered manifest.

JSON Schema and OpenAPI-compatible serialized artifacts are generated deterministically rather than maintained as divergent handwritten schemas.
Registry storage is behind PersistenceProvider: Local and Self-hosted `simple` use SQLite, while Self-hosted `server` and managed-cloud use PostgreSQL.
Public consumers use versioned API/SDK contracts rather than registry tables or internal database schemas.

columns.Extracted independently checkable clause: Define the concrete security and protocol boundaries among Agent HQ Cloud, a selected Control Plane deployment, and Local/Self-hosted RuntimeNodes.

This document removes ambiguity around desktop packaging, direct co-located execution, Agent HQ remote product control, Runtime Gateway transport, Self-hosted nodes, local project access, and optional ContextProvider access.
Developer MVP uses direct local Control Plane-to-RuntimeDriver execution by default.
Agent HQ Remote Relay is used when web/mobile must reach a selected Local/Self-hosted Control Plane;
Runtime Gateway is used only when that Control Plane must reach a different/non-co-located RuntimeNode.
No local provider is required for baseline RuntimeNode or execution behavior.

Agent HQ application services own RuntimeNode registration, stable runtime_node_id, account association, workspace authorization, pairing state, authentication/signing public-key metadata, distinct E2E encryption public-key metadata, credential/key rotation and revocation, user-visible node metadata, and audit history.
Agent HQ Cloud never receives the corresponding private keys.

The separate Control Plane owns RuntimeConnection records, negotiated runtime capabilities/freshness, runtime health used for eligibility, deterministic routing decisions, RuntimeAdapter policy, optional ContextProviderConnection/capability/health records and ContextProviderAdapter policy, local or remote runtime-command reconciliation, and normalized execution/runtime/provider events.
Remote Runtime Gateway command records exist only when a non-co-located RuntimeNode is used.
Agent HQ does not read Control Plane runtime or provider tables directly.
The desktop Local Runtime Host is a trusted device component acting for one registered RuntimeNode.

It protects the node's distinct authentication/signing and E2E decryption keys plus any Agent HQ local-content key handles, and performs only authenticated, authorized commands addressed to that node.
A RuntimeDriver is the node-side implementation that performs concrete managed-runtime, ACP (Agent Client Protocol), filesystem, process, credential, or Artifact-transfer operations.
A ContextProviderDriver is a separate optional node-side driver family for already-authorized local provider health, bounded read, cancellation, and separately permitted write operations.
Neither owns selection, routing, context policy, product authorization, provider scope, or memory policy.
Agent HQ clients consume normalized node, runtime, and optional provider read models.
They do not receive raw RuntimeNode or provider credentials, loopback endpoints, local/database paths, harness credentials, provider corpus or native memory, or native process handles.
A ContentSyncDevice is a separate Agent HQ product-content synchronization identity governed by ADR-037.
A `user_client` kind represents a desktop/browser/mobile client;
a `content_authority` kind represents a Local/Self-hosted encrypted content authority and may be co-located with a RuntimeNode.

Registering either kind does not create RuntimeNode execution authority or expose RuntimeNode credentials, and RuntimeNode pairing does not automatically authorize access to durable synchronized ContentReplicas.

The authenticated desktop client requests a short-lived pairing challenge from Agent HQ application services.
The Local Runtime Host generates an Ed25519 authentication/signing key pair and a distinct static X25519 E2E remote-content encryption key pair for RemoteContentEnvelope command/result transport.
Private keys are stored in the operating-system secure credential store and are never uploaded or reused across credential roles.
This RuntimeNode X25519 key is not the ContentSyncDevice key used for durable synchronized-content decryption.

The device signs the pairing challenge with its Ed25519 key and submits the signing/authentication public key, X25519 encryption public key/key ID, platform, application version, and requested ownership scope.

Agent HQ verifies the challenge, creates the RuntimeNode record, binds the signing/authentication and encryption public-key metadata, records the approving user, and returns the stable runtime_node_id.
The node obtains short-lived transport/channel credentials by proving possession of its Ed25519 authentication key.
The X25519 key is used only for E2E content decryption/encryption contexts and never substitutes for channel authentication.
Long-lived bearer secrets are not stored in normal application data.
Pairing challenges and one-time codes have strict expiry, single-use semantics, audience binding, and CSRF/state protection.
Signing/authentication and encryption key rotation are independent.
A replacement key is verified/registered before the previous key is retired.
Revoking the signing/authentication key invalidates channel credentials;
revoking an encryption key blocks new E2E payloads to that key immediately.
A previous encryption private key may remain node-local only for the bounded queued-envelope grace window, no longer than 24 hours or the owning command expiry.
RuntimeNode signing/authentication and E2E remote-content encryption private keys are non-exportable where platform APIs allow it and otherwise stored in the OS keychain or equivalent secure storage.
They are separate keys with separate identifiers and permitted uses.
ContentSyncDevice synchronization keys and ContentKeyEpoch material are outside the RuntimeNode credential model and cannot authenticate a RuntimeNode or remote command channel.
RuntimeNode transport credentials and public-key records are scoped to one node and permitted account/workspace relationships.
They are not equivalent to an end-user session, Control Plane service credential, E2E private key, or provider/harness credential.

Agent HQ stores signing/authentication and encryption public keys, key identifiers/fingerprints, credential role, lifecycle status, created_at, rotated_at, revoked_at, and last successful proof where applicable.
Private material never enters cloud persistence.
Short-lived access tokens include runtime_node_id, allowed audiences, issued_at, expires_at, and a confirmation claim bound to the device public key.
All credential use, rotation, revocation, and failed proofs are auditable without logging private material or reusable tokens.

For co-located desktop execution, the local Control Plane communicates with the Local Runtime Host/RuntimeDrivers through DirectLocalRuntimeTransport over an allowlisted local IPC or in-process boundary and does not require a cloud connection.

Agent HQ web/mobile remote control is a separate product-to-Control-Plane transport: the selected Local/Self-hosted host opens outbound authenticated connectivity to Agent HQ's durable relay, which routes metadata-only commands or E2E ciphertext.
Runtime Gateway is used only when a Control Plane must reach a different non-co-located RuntimeNode.
No remote service requires an unrestricted inbound port on the user's device or connects directly to an arbitrary loopback runtime or ContextProvider endpoint.
Remote relay/gateway server identity is established by TLS.
RuntimeNode transport identity is established by a short-lived credential plus Ed25519 possession proof.
The remote service revalidates node status and authorization on connection and periodically thereafter.
Content confidentiality for Agent HQ remote control is additionally protected by the separate HPKE envelope and does not rely on the relay being able to decrypt payloads.
This channel is separate from the HTTP plus SSE product-state transport.
WebSockets are used here because privileged RuntimeNode control is bidirectional, long-lived, and command-oriented.
The same secure transport may carry adapter-owned commands for runtime drivers and optional local ContextProvider drivers;
their semantic contracts and authorities remain distinct.
A RuntimeNode has at most one active logical session per remote transport role/endpoint.
Reconnect uses a session identifier and last acknowledged sequence;
a newer authenticated session supersedes an older stale connection.
Remote heartbeat defaults to 15 seconds, the connection is degraded after two missed heartbeats, and the node is offline after three misses/45 seconds.
The Runtime Gateway is an independently deployable remote-node transport service.
It maintains long-lived connections and bounded per-node state when the selected controller and RuntimeNode are not co-located;
it is not required in the ordinary local desktop execution path and does not share ordinary Agent HQ request-handler lifetimes.
Every runtime-channel message uses a versioned envelope containing at least:
protocol_version
message_type
message_id
runtime_node_id
workspace_id when the operation is workspace scoped
command_id for command, acknowledgement, cancellation, event, and result correlation
execution_id and attempt_id where applicable
command_family and driver_type, such as runtime or context_provider, without embedding a concrete provider into the core envelope
context_provider_connection_id and memory_write_proposal_id where applicable
idempotency_key for effect-producing commands
issued_at and expires_at
connection_sequence and command_sequence
trace_id and request_id
payload_schema_version
payload
hello and hello_ack: protocol negotiation, node status, supported channel capabilities, optional driver families, and resume position
heartbeat and heartbeat_ack: liveness, clock-skew detection, version, runtime and optional local-provider health, and capability deltas
command: authorized request to invoke a RuntimeDriver or ContextProviderDriver operation under an adapter-owned payload schema
ack: durable acknowledgement that the node accepted or rejected a command for processing
event: normalized progress or state change for an accepted command
result: terminal success or classified failure
cancel: idempotent cancellation request for an active command or execution
error: channel-level protocol or authorization failure that is not a runtime result
Transport delivery is at least once.
The Local Runtime Host and selected node-side driver deduplicate `command_id` and `idempotency_key` so one approved node command is dispatched once logically.
RuntimeDrivers and ContextProviderDrivers must propagate an idempotency key or use an authoritative status check for downstream effect-producing operations.
ContextProvider retrieval is read-only and never writes memory.
When a downstream operation is non-idempotent and its outcome is ambiguous, the driver must not retry automatically;
it returns `reconciliation_required` for explicit status recovery or user review.
The node persists a bounded command ledger containing command_id, idempotency_key, state, terminal result reference, and expiry.
Terminal remote runtime/relay command records are retained at least 7 days.
A duplicate command returns the existing acknowledgement or result while retained.
Commands are rejected when expired, addressed to another node/workspace, outside the negotiated protocol/schema version, incompatible with current permissions, or oversized.
Remote start/control commands expire no later than 24 hours and never outlive their owning InteractionRequest.
Ordinary Runtime Gateway frames and Agent HQ E2E ciphertext payloads are capped at 1 MiB;
larger content uses authorized references, a separately bounded transfer protocol, or Artifact promotion.
A remote gateway does not consider a command accepted until it receives ack.
The local direct path uses the same logical acknowledgement/idempotency semantics.
Lost acknowledgements may cause safe redelivery of the same command_id.
Cancellation is idempotent and races with terminal completion deterministically.
A terminal result wins over a later cancellation request.
Remote reconnect resumes from acknowledged sequence where possible.
The controlling Control Plane reconciles non-terminal commands against node/runtime status rather than assuming that a dropped connection means failure.
Local Control Plane/process restart uses the same durable command ledger and reconciliation principles without requiring a cloud reconnect.
A local-only execution or required local ContextProvider request is never silently reassigned to another RuntimeNode, provider, or cloud environment.
Rerouting or provider substitution requires an explicit Control Plane policy decision;
runtime reassignment creates a new attempt, while context-provider substitution creates a new contribution and ContextPackage version.

A retry may reuse the same package only when policy confirms that its ProjectState, authorization, provider mapping, provider contribution revisions/digests, freshness, and degradation state remain valid.
Required-provider unavailability or revoked scope cannot be silently converted into a stale cached package.
A changed package receives a new version and is recorded on the new attempt.
